scenario.title: Speed policy comparison (Gen2 step)
scenario.description: Same hardware as S01, but the speed-change policy is set to gen2_step: true. Instead of Gen1 -> Gen3 -> Gen4, each downstream port steps through every rate: Gen1 -> Gen2 -> Gen3 -> Gen4. The final result is identical; the path and the time to reach the final speed are not.
scenario.symptom: Same final state as the healthy baseline, but the bring-up takes a little longer.

expected.summary: Every populated link visits L0 at Gen1, Gen2, Gen3 and Gen4 (three speed changes instead of two) and ends as in S01.

scenario.what_to_look_for: Four green L0 segments per link instead of three. The extra step (Gen1 -> Gen2) has no teal equalization bar because 5.0 GT/s does not equalize. Compare time_to_final_speed_ns for link A with S01 (13.726 ms in S01): the extra Recovery pass costs a little time. Equalization still runs exactly once per rate at 8 and 16 GT/s.
scenario.what_this_means: How a link climbs to its final rate is a policy choice (hardware autonomous behavior, firmware, or software through Target Link Speed and Retrain Link). In the model the downstream port always initiates speed changes; on real links either port may. The ending state is what LnkSta shows; the path is only visible in a trace. When comparing two platforms, a different path does not mean a problem.
likely_root_causes: Different root port or switch firmware policies for speed changes (normal).
Software stepping the Target Link Speed during bring-up.
how_to_debug: If bring-up time matters, measure time from PERST# deassertion to DL_Link_Active and to the final speed on both platforms.
Use this model to compare policies: run S01 and S13 and compare the counters.
mystery_hints: Count the L0 segments on one swimlane.
scenario.mystery_cause: The speed-change policy steps through every rate (Gen1 -> Gen2 -> Gen3 -> Gen4).
